subject_session: 15 sessions from 5 mice (LA3, LA8, LA9, LA11, LA12); example sub-LA11_ses-1

headline_stat.name: fraction of units significantly frequency-tuned (KW p<0.01, rate>=0.5Hz)

justification.dataset: DANDI 000986 mouse auditory cortex pure-tone Neuropixels is the canonical dataset for frequency tuning, an expert choice.
justification.handling: Data correctly streamed and trial-aligned with a sound windowed-count scheme, but unit inclusion is only a 0.5 Hz rate floor with no spike-sorting quality criteria.
justification.analysis: Kruskal-Wallis across frequencies plus a Poisson GLM complement is appropriate and correct, though the ~7400-trial test is heavily overpowered and no effect-size or shuffle control tempers the tuned-fraction claim.
justification.correctness: Reported values (frac 0.853, bf_counts summing to 1221, median selectivity 0.41, 96% within-octave) reproduce internally, are consistent with the figures, and are physically possible.
justification.figures: Figures are clearly labeled with units and sample sizes and show the effect convincingly, with example curves honestly chosen by significance rather than for flattering shape.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate and examples are labeled honestly, but the write-up states no limitation, notably that the huge trial count inflates the significant-tuned fraction, so it sits at a clean-result 3 rather than 4.
justification.verdict: Core work is sound, the phenomenon is clearly demonstrated, and both hard-rule axes clear the bar, so this is acceptable rotation-student work.
